title: Macroeconomic Impacts of China’s Energy Transition
abstract: Solar and wind power account for a growing share of electricity generation in China and now dominate new capacity additions. As the power system transitions toward renewable generation, greater flexibility will be required to maintain system stability. This paper uses a computable general equilibrium model to assess the macroeconomic implications of this transition. Model results indicate a modest increase in electricity prices in the near-term, followed by sustained declines as renewable shares rise, particularly when variability is managed through battery storage rather than coal-fired backup generation. While the transition requires substantial adjustments in electricity supply and investment, it raises GDP in the long run and strengthens energy security. Battery-based flexibility outperforms continued reliance on coal across multiple dimensions, even when accounting for rising electricity demand from emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence. However, this transition pathway also increases the risk of stranded assets in the coal power sector.
abstract_zh: 太阳能和风能在中国发电量中所占份额日益增长，并且目前在新增装机容量中占据主导地位。随着电力系统向可再生能源发电转型，需要更大的灵活性来维持系统稳定。本文利用一个可计算一般均衡模型，评估这一转型的宏观经济影响。模型结果表明，近期电价将小幅上涨，随后随着可再生能源份额的提高而持续下降，尤其是当波动性通过储能电池而非燃煤备用发电来管理时。尽管这一转型需要对电力供应和投资进行大幅调整，但它从长期看会提高GDP，并增强能源安全。即便考虑到人工智能等新兴技术带来的电力需求增长，以电池为基础的灵活性方案在多个维度上仍优于继续依赖煤炭。然而，这一转型路径也增加了煤电行业资产搁浅的风险。

title: Trade wars and trade disputes: The role of equity and political support
IMF-ENV: Integrating Climate, Energy, and Trade Policies in a General Equilibrium Framework
abstract: IMF-ENV is a global dynamic computable general equilibrium (CGE) model developed by the IMF's Research Department. The model features a database of 160 countries and regions, along with 76 sectors, and can be calibrated to a wide range of country-sector combinations. The model's general equilibrium structure, combined with its high level of detail, enables it to assess both direct and indirect domestic structural changes and cross-border spillover effects of policies. This makes it suitable for examining the medium- and long-term macroeconomic effects as well as structural shifts arising from national and/or global climate mitigation, energy, fiscal and trade policies. The model reports impact on macroeconomic variables, sectoral outcomes, employment and bilateral trade flows, along with detailed information for energy demand and supply, electricity generation and GHG emissions.
abstract_zh: IMF-ENV是由国际货币基金组织研究部开发的全球动态可计算一般均衡（CGE）模型。该模型包含160个国家和地区的数据库，以及76个部门，可以针对多种国家-部门组合进行校准。该模型的一般均衡结构与其高度细致的刻画相结合，使其能够评估政策的直接和间接国内结构变化以及跨境溢出效应。这使其适合于考察国家和/或全球气候减缓、能源、财政和贸易政策所产生的中长期宏观经济效应以及结构性转变。该模型报告了对宏观经济变量、部门结果、就业和双边贸易流量的影响，并提供能源需求与供应、电力生产和温室气体排放的详细信息。

title: The ENV-FIBA Model for Climate Risk Analysis: Framework, Model Details and Guide
abstract: We present the ENV-FIBA macro-micro model framework that can be used to analyze the climate-macro-financial consequences of climate scenarios and related policy counterfactuals. The model consists of a multi-country Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) core and a connected micro simulation module for an economy’s individual nonfinancial firms and banks. The climate-macro-financial scenario simulations are anchored in future temperature and emission pathways, alongside policy assumptions regarding carbon taxation, fiscal revenue recycling and reinvestment, optional carbon border adjustment mechanisms, and others. We illustrate the use of the model for Japan. We emphasize, exemplify with the model, and recommend in general: (1) that physical and transition risk effects be modeled jointly to a maximal extent (given their intertwined nature); (2) that it is important to consider bank balance sheets that are dynamic (not static), to capture the differential growth of emmission intensive industries that may shrink, opposed to those that may flourish; and (3) related to the latter, that such dynamically evolving lending has primary impacts on bank solvency via interest income, along with quantitatively often smaller impacts through loan losses from borrower defaults.
abstract_zh: 我们提出了ENV-FIBA宏观—微观模型框架，可用于分析气候情景及相关政策反事实的气候—宏观—金融后果。该模型由一个多国可计算一般均衡（CGE）核心，以及与之相连的、针对一个经济体内各非金融企业和银行的微观模拟模块组成。气候—宏观—金融情景模拟以未来的温度和排放路径为基础，并结合有关碳税、财政收入循环利用与再投资、可选的碳边境调节机制等方面的政策假设。我们以日本为例说明该模型的应用。我们强调并以模型加以示范，并一般性地建议：（1）尽可能联合建模物理风险和转型风险的效应（鉴于二者相互交织的性质）；（2）重要的是考虑动态而非静态的银行资产负债表，以刻画那些可能萎缩的排放密集型产业与那些可能繁荣的产业之间的差异化增长；（3）与此相关，动态演变的贷款首先通过利息收入对银行偿付能力产生主要影响，而通过借款人违约造成的贷款损失，其影响在数量上通常较小。

title: Climate Transition Risk and Financial Stability in France
abstract: This study empirically investigates the impact of the climate transition on the French financial sector using a micro-macro approach to examine the long-term effects of climate mitigation and decarbonization policies on sectoral output and the effects on firm profitability and the likelihood of corporate defaults. We employ a recursive-dynamic, multi-regional, multi-sectoral computable general equilibrium (CGE) model to simulate the Fit-for-55 climate scenario and then integrate the sectoral output paths derived from the model into firm-level corporate balance sheets and risks. We then assess the extent of credit exposure of banks to energy-intensive sectors. Our findings indicate that, under the Fit-for-55 scenario, the mining, chemicals and manufacturing sectors might face notable increases in their probability of defaults, in turn creating pockets of vulnerabilities in some parts of the banking system depending on their exposure to these energy-intensive sectors. This highlights the importance for a timely and orderly transition, including integrating climate transition plans into the prudential framework.
abstract_zh: 本研究采用微观—宏观相结合的方法，实证考察了气候转型对法国金融部门的影响，以检验气候减缓和脱碳政策对部门产出的长期效应，以及对企业盈利能力和企业违约可能性的影响。我们采用递归动态、多区域、多部门的可计算一般均衡（CGE）模型来模拟“一揽子55”（Fit-for-55）气候情景，然后将模型得出的部门产出路径整合到企业层面的资产负债表和风险之中。随后，我们评估了银行对能源密集型部门的信贷敞口程度。我们的研究发现表明，在“一揽子55”情景下，采矿、化工和制造业部门可能面临违约概率的显著上升，进而根据银行体系对这些能源密集型部门的敞口程度，在银行体系的某些部分形成脆弱性集中区。这凸显了及时、有序的转型的重要性，包括将气候转型计划纳入审慎监管框架。

title: Medium-term Macroeconomic Effects of Russia’s War in Ukraine and How it Affects Energy Security and Global Emission Targets
abstract: Russia’s war in Ukraine has disrupted the supply of natural gas for many European countries, triggering an energy crisis and affecting energy security. We simulate the medium-term effects of these trade disruptions and find that most European countries have limited GDP losses but those more dependent on Russian natural gas face moderate losses. European fossil fuel consumption and emissions are reduced and after accounting for the war impacts, achieving Europe’s emission targets becomes slightly less costly. In terms of energy security, the war eliminates European energy dependency from Russian imports, but most of the natural gas and oil imports will be substituted by other suppliers. We also find that constructing a new Russian pipeline to China does not provide significant macroeconomic benefits to either country.
abstract_zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争扰乱了许多欧洲国家的天然气供应，引发了能源危机并影响了能源安全。我们模拟了这些贸易中断的中期效应，发现大多数欧洲国家的GDP损失有限，但那些更依赖俄罗斯天然气的国家面临中等程度的损失。欧洲的化石燃料消费和排放有所减少，并且在计入战争影响之后，实现欧洲的排放目标的成本略有降低。就能源安全而言，战争消除了欧洲对俄罗斯进口的能源依赖，但大部分天然气和石油进口将被其他供应商替代。我们还发现，修建一条通往中国的新俄罗斯管道，对两国的宏观经济都没有带来显著收益。

title: A Ricardian Trade Structure in CGE: Modeling Eaton-Kortum Based Trade with GTAP
EU Trade Sustainability Impact Assessments: Revisiting the Consultation Process
abstract: Trade sustainability impact assessments (SIAs) are the main tool used by the European Commission to assess the potential effects of trade policy initiatives and to engage with stakeholders. SIAs have two elements: a model-based quantitative analysis and a consultation process. Both include a focus on a broad range of non-trade issues, many of which are included in sustainable development chapters of EU trade agreements. This paper argues for making consultation processes a more useful input into the design of trade cooperation. Scaled responses to a survey with closed end questions on a broad range of non-trade policy objectives combined with deliberative polling of a representative sample of survey respondents could help identify what stakeholders in the EU and partner countries perceive to be priority non-trade objectives, as well as issue-specific baselines, performance targets and appropriate instruments to apply. Building bridges between a revamped ex ante consultation process and mechanisms that encompass public and private actors to support implementation, resolve problems and assess progress over time could further help achieve trade and sustainable development goals.
abstract_zh: 贸易可持续性影响评估（SIAs）是欧盟委员会用来评估贸易政策倡议潜在影响并与利益相关者开展互动的主要工具。SIAs包含两个要素：基于模型的定量分析和协商程序。两者都重点关注广泛的非贸易议题，其中许多议题被纳入欧盟贸易协定的可持续发展章节。本文主张使协商程序成为贸易合作设计中更有用的投入。对涵盖广泛非贸易政策目标的封闭式问题进行量化问卷调查，并结合对调查受访者代表性样本进行的协商式民意测验（deliberative polling），有助于识别欧盟及其伙伴国的利益相关者认为的优先非贸易目标，以及具体议题的基准、绩效目标和适用工具。将经过革新的事前协商程序，与动员公共和私营行为体以支持实施、解决问题并长期评估进展的机制相结合，将进一步有助于实现贸易与可持续发展目标。

A Stochastic Indicator for Sovereign Debt Sustainability
abstract: We propose a stochastic indicator to assess government debt sustainability. This indicator combines the effect of economic uncertainty – represented by stochastic simulations of interest and growth rates – with the expected fiscal response, which provides information on the long-term country-specific attitude towards fiscal sustainability. We apply our framework to postwar data for nine OECD countries and find that our indicator – the potential increase in debt in bad states of the world – distinguishes countries that have sustainability concerns (Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Iceland) from those that do not (the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany).
abstract_zh: 我们提出了一个用于评估政府债务可持续性的随机指标。该指标将经济不确定性的影响（通过对利率和增长率的随机模拟来表示）与预期的财政反应相结合，后者反映了长期以来各国对财政可持续性的特定态度。我们将该框架应用于九个经合组织（OECD）国家的战后数据，发现我们的指标——即在不利世界状态下债务的潜在增幅——能够将存在可持续性担忧的国家（意大利、西班牙、葡萄牙和冰岛）与不存在此类担忧的国家（美国、英国、荷兰、比利时和德国）区分开来。

title: Stochastic debt sustainability indicators
abstract: This paper proposes indicators to assess government debt sustainability in the medium and long term. We follow the methodological approach by Bohn (2008) and distinguish three channels that contribute to sustainable government finances: economic growth, real interest payments and fiscal responses. We combine the estimated fiscal response with a stochastic debt simulation to create two indicators. The first captures the probability of debt-to-GDP ratios rising by more than 20 percentage points during a 10-year period. A government will fail on this indicator if its fiscal response to an increase in debt is not sufficient to control the swings in debt caused by shocks to real growth and interest payments. The second indicator captures the probability of debt levels being above 90% of GDP in 10 years. We estimate these indicators using historical data for nine OECD countries. We find that the probability of debt-to-GDP ratios rising by more than 20 percentage points in the next decade clearly identifies countries that have sustainability concerns: Italy, Spain, Portugal and Iceland, from those that do not: US, UK, Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.JEL Classification: E4, E6, H0, H6
abstract_zh: 本文提出了用于评估中长期政府债务可持续性的指标。我们遵循Bohn（2008）的方法论路径，区分出三条有助于政府财政可持续的渠道：经济增长、实际利息支付和财政反应。我们将估计的财政反应与随机债务模拟相结合，构造了两个指标。第一个指标衡量在10年期内债务与GDP之比上升超过20个百分点的概率。如果政府对债务增加的财政反应不足以控制由实际增长和利息支付冲击所引起的债务波动，那么该政府在这一指标上将不及格。第二个指标衡量10年后债务水平超过GDP的90%的概率。我们利用九个经合组织国家的历史数据估计了这些指标。我们发现，未来十年内债务与GDP之比上升超过20个百分点的概率，能够清楚地将存在可持续性担忧的国家（意大利、西班牙、葡萄牙和冰岛）与不存在此类担忧的国家（美国、英国、荷兰、比利时和德国）区分开来。JEL分类号：E4, E6, H0, H6
